originality.rationale: The inspected primary literature addresses BDF2 monotonicity, startup and finite-step positivity. The nearest public scalar stage-index result changes index at fixed step with backward-Euler startup; this theorem fixes index, varies timestep, and uses exact startup, proves a strict all-stage phase monotonicity and deduces arbitrarily many separated graph-star loss windows. Different one-step heat transfer methods with analogous diagonal bounds do not imply these exact BDF2 zeros. Publication priority is qualified by possible older unindexed recurrence analyses.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical scalar-oscillation or asymptotic recurrence literature may contain an equivalent fixed-index exact-start phase-zero classification under another name.
Search coverage and source inspections do not establish global priority or mathematical independence; published monotonicity results provide substantial background.
The proof establishes a lower bound on distinct finite-star negativity windows but no exhaustive fixed-star classification.

value.rationale: Unlike a small isolated sign counterexample, the all-stage theorem gives the exact number of zero crossings for every k, a structural growth law for arbitrarily many separated nonnegative/negative return regimes on finite graph diffusion, and the sharp smallest network dimension witnessing stage-two diagonal loss. These quantify a natural time-integration positivity failure that finite timestep sweeps and scalar A-stability do not capture. The graph-size result is not presented as a general off-diagonal positivity classification.
